chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Sandal, from Yasser, from Al-Yasa' ibn Hamza, who said:

I was in the gathering of Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him), narrating to him, and a large crowd had gathered to him, asking him about the Halal and the Haram. Then a tall, fair-skinned man entered and said: 'Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah! I am a man from your lovers and the lovers of your fathers and forefathers (peace be upon them). I have returned from Hajj, and my expenses are lost, and I have nothing with me to reach a stage (of travel). So if you see fit, advance me to my city. By Allah, it would be a favor upon me. So when I reach my city, I will give in charity that which you command me to give on your behalf, for I am not a recipient of charity.'

He said to him: 'Sit, may Allah have mercy on you!' And he turned to the people, narrating to them until they dispersed. He remained with Suleiman Al-Ja'fari, Khaysama, and myself. He said: 'Do you allow me to enter?' Suleiman said to him: 'May Allah advance your affair.' So he arose and entered the chamber and remained for a while. Then he came out, closed the door, and put his hand out from the top of the door and said: 'Where is the Khurasani man?' He said: 'Here I am.' He said: 'Take these two hundred Dinars and be assisted by them in your provisions and expenses, and be blessed by them, and do not give charity with them on my behalf. Go, so that I do not see you and you do not see me.'

Then he came out. Suleiman said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! You have been generous and merciful, so why did you veil your face from him?' He said: 'Out of fear that I might see the humiliation of asking in his face, for fulfilling his need. Have you not heard the Hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'The one who conceals a good deed equals seventy Hajj, and the one who publicizes a bad deed is forsaken, and the one who conceals it is forgiven for it'? Have you not heard the words of the ancients: 'Whenever I go to Him to seek a need, I return to my family with my face undamaged'.'

key_terms.الْمُذِيعُ بِالسَّيِّئَةِ: The one who publicizes a bad deed
key_terms.الْمُسْتَتِرُ بِالْحَسَنَةِ: The one who conceals a good deed

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of concealing charity in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) demonstrates the Shia emphasis on *khusūf* (concealment) by discreetly providing two hundred Dinars to a pilgrim, ensuring the man’s dignity remained intact by avoiding public scrutiny. This act is rooted in the Prophetic tradition that concealing charity equals seventy Hajj pilgrimages, highlighting the spiritual merit of preserving the recipient's self-respect over mere material transfer. The narrative underscores the scholarly principle that the etiquette of giving (*ādāb al-ṣadaqah*) requires sensitivity to the recipient's emotional state, a key theme in Shia ethical jurisprudence.
